name: Stakeholder and Buying Center Influence Mapping (B2B)
phase: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [Role A] controls purchase authority, while [Role B] serves as an internal champion. We will verify this by mapping the buying center dynamics across 8 enterprise target accounts, and consider it validated if the operational economic buyer matches our target persona in ≥ 75% of evaluated org charts.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Define the six buying roles: economic buyer, champion, end user, technical gatekeeper, procurement, blocker.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Call across departments in each account and ask whose budget pays and who holds the veto in review.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Chart the decision, veto and capital-authorisation path for each of the eight accounts.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Define the six canonical enterprise purchasing roles: Economic Buyer, Champion, End User, Technical Gatekeeper, Procurement, and Blocker.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Conduct organizational discovery calls across multiple departments within each target account. Ask: "Whose departmental budget pays for this solution?" "Who possesses absolute veto authority during procurement and security review?".

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Chart the formal decision, veto, and capital authorization pathways for each enterprise account.

warning.label: Champion Conflation
warning.text: An enthusiastic end user is mistaken for the economic buyer, and the deal stalls at procurement.

warningFull: Founders routinely mistake an enthusiastic end-user champion for the economic buyer, discovering too late that the deal stalls indefinitely when presented to procurement.
